text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Austrian Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger may have to draw up further austerity measures to keep the state budget defict on track in 1997 and 1998. Lower than expected revenues mean central government's budget could overshoot the planned 68 billion schillings by around 12 billion. A 36 billion schillings hole could be blown out of the 1998 budget.
- The government coalition parties and two opposition parties have agreed on a reform of politicians' wages in July.

- Die Erste savings bank, which has just taken over the City of Vienna's stake in GiroCredit, plans to bid for the state's stake in postal savings bank PSK. Die Erste's new chief Andreas Treichl plans to raise the two banks earnings "massively".
- Industry is blocking reform of trade regulations saying it will only agree should tax advantages for farmers be abolished.

- Investor Kapital & Wert will raise its dividend to 48 schillings from 28 on record earnings. It now plans to sell off its stake in electronic retailer Koeck as it could take over another electrical goods retailer Niedermeyer.
- Papermaker Frantschach wants to take over Poland's biggest paper production plant in Swiecie which is due to be privatised soon.
- The government coalition parties have passed a reform of Austria's working hour regulations and have loosened the ban on Sunday working despite protests by opposition parties and the church.

- Die Erste savings bank will pay 8.2 billion schillings for GiroCredit within a year. A capital increase is planned to pay for the takeover. Three foreign subsidiaries of Bank Austria and Creditanstalt will be added.
- The finance ministry is losing up to 10 billion schillings through insolvencies because it is not demanding payment of taxes in time, the audit office criticises.
